name: Bright moss
lede: Bright moss is ColorHub's name for Hiwamo'egi (鶸萌黄), a traditional Japanese color meaning "siskin sprout yellow-green," after the siskin finch and new plant shoots.

sections.title: Hiwamo'egi, a finch's sprout-color
sections.body:
The Wikipedia survey "Traditional colors of Japan" lists this color under the romanized name Hiwamo'egi, written 鶸萌黄 [1]. The library glosses the kanji as "siskin sprout yellow": 鶸 names the siskin, a small yellow-green finch, and 萌黄 is the yellow-green of a new plant shoot [1]. No book consulted here independently dates or expands the name, so its earlier history is undocumented [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[bright-moss]], [[ugly-green]], [[avocado]] and [[swedish-green]], at 3.6, 3.6, 3.6 and 4.2 ΔE [1]. The hex given here, #7A942E, is a modern screen approximation fit to that gloss, not a measured pigment or dye [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
A color within range of this swatch appears in 33 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.14 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 13 [2]. That makes it rarer than 65 percent of the named colors we track [2].

It peaks in the 1800s, present in 9 of 8,345 paintings from that century, 1.5 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in more than three-quarters of the paintings that carry it, never a dominant field [2]. The earliest dated appearance we have is 1840, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a true first sighting [2].

origin.named_after: siskin sprout yellow, from 鶸 (siskin finch) and 萌黄 (new-shoot yellow-green)
